---
status: accepted
---

# Character derivatives are sub-identities: referenced as `@[角色/衍生]` (`@[character/derivative]`); derivative asset images are generated by editing the base asset image or replaced by an author upload

A character has only one asset image, which cannot express the same person's change of outfit, transformation, or disguise. Decision: a derivative is a sub-identity attached under a character, sharing the character's name, voice, speaker binding, and position in the global namespace; the character entry keeps its existing fields as the base, and derivatives are stored in a `derivatives` table within the character entry, keyed by derivative name, with derivative names unique only within their owning character. Scripts reference them as `@[角色/衍生]` (`@[character/derivative]`), and the `characters_in_*` arrays of the storyboard route use the same string; `/` is already a forbidden character in asset names, so the notation is unambiguous. The `speaker` field accepts only the base name; when a derivative is written in the speaker position of the body, it belongs to the base and binds only the voice. The mechanism is modelled generically per AssetSpec, and this decision enables it only for character.

**Derivatives have no original image; the asset image can be generated or replaced by upload.** A derivative holds only a description of the change in appearance relative to the base and one asset image. A generated asset image is an image edit of the base asset image (ADR 0050 semantics), with the change description as the edit instruction; after the base asset image is regenerated, generated derivative asset images are judged stale and not automatically regenerated; a derivative asset image cannot be generated when the base has no asset image. The author can also upload an image to replace the derivative asset image, through the same entry as uploading the base asset image; the uploaded image becomes the derivative's current version and enters version history. An uploaded derivative asset image is a finished product and is registered by the image itself (see `docs/adr/0062`): regenerating the base asset image, changing the base or derivative description, or changing the art style does not make it stale; switching to a generated version returns to the basis of editing the base asset image, and restoring the uploaded version registers it by the image itself again. Uploading does not depend on the base asset image. Uploading only replaces the asset image and is not used as the base image for further edit generation, so the derivative still has no original image. The character appearance in storyboard and video prompts = base description + the current form's change description, even if the asset image was uploaded.

**Choosing forms within the same entry**: no limit. Each referenced base or derivative injects one asset image (whether the base and a derivative appear together in the same shot, or several derivatives appear together), and the prompt explains that they are different forms of the same character; whatever references the author wrote are injected, so shots such as before and after a transformation in the same frame can be expressed.

**Disk layout**: `characters/derivatives/{角色}/{衍生}.png` (`{character}/{derivative}`), with version history in `versions/characters/derivatives/{角色}/`. A character can be named `refs`, so derivatives can't be placed directly under `characters/{角色}/`. Renaming a character moves the directory, and renaming a derivative changes the file stem; both are included in the cascading rename transaction of ADR 0057. The artifact manifest key is `(character, "角色/衍生")` (`character/derivative`).

**The global asset library** carries derivatives in the child table `asset_derivatives`, moving in and out as a set with the character, and the conflict strategy `rename` changes only the character name. Derivative asset images brought into a project from the library are finished products and are registered by the image itself (see `docs/adr/0062`): regenerating the base asset image or changing the base or derivative description doesn't make them stale; after regenerating in the project, they return to the basis of editing the base asset image.

## Explicitly not adopted

- **Registering derivatives as independent characters + a "same person" association marker**: zero schema change, but speaker, reference audio, and identity description would have to be maintained repeatedly across multiple entries, and the agent would treat them as two people; conflicts with the definition "character = a specific identity".
- **Everything is a form, migrating the base into a derivative named `默认` (Default) as well**: a more symmetric model, at the cost of a schema migration, moving files, re-keying the artifact manifest, and rewriting all existing scripts; the asymmetry of the base being the "resident appearance" already holds in creative practice.
- **Derivative description written as the full appearance, replacing the base description**: duplicates the base's description of facial features and build, and loses the generation semantics of "editing based on the base".
- **Uploading a base image for a derivative and then generating by editing with the change description**: amounts to giving the derivative an original image; the generation basis would have to choose between the base asset image and the derivative original, and the UI would gain an extra original-image slot. What users want is to swap in a satisfactory image directly when the generated result doesn't look right, which uploading to replace the asset image already satisfies.
- **Derivatives with their own voice_style or reference audio**: voice belongs to identity; a form whose voice has changed is another character.
- **Using `#`, `·`, or `-` as the separator**: all are valid asset-name characters, making parsing ambiguous.

## Consequences

- The project schema version is bumped; `derivatives` defaults to an empty table, and existing projects need no rewriting.
- The set of character names in validation expands from a flat set of names to "base names ∪ base name/derivative name"; `_unregistered_refs` remains the single entry point for equivalence judgement.
- Asset breakdown (analyze-assets) takes on derivative recognition, with the criteria written in that agent's definition; script_plan / prompt_authoring write `@[角色/衍生]` (`@[character/derivative]`) according to the plot state.
- The storyboard reference popup, avatar stack, and asset card must all be able to present derivatives; the derivative entry on the asset card is a button that opens a popover for viewing and editing derivatives.
